def next_move_in_chess(game, moves_so_far, previous_move):
    """
    This function takes a game and the moves made so far as input, and returns
    the next move in the format as defined in the problem.

    Args:
        game : str
            The current state of the game.
        moves_so_far : list
            The list of moves made so far.
        previous_move : str
            The previously made move.

    Returns:
        str
            The next move in the game.

    """
    # Define the illegal board positions
    illegal_positions = [
        "Kingside Castling - d4 (= p-king4), g5 (= p-g8/7), h3 (= p-h7/6), h6 (= p-h4/5), h7 (= p-h8/7), Kg1 (= K-g1), Kgf1 (= K-g7/6), Kgxh2xg2 (= K-g8/7), Kg2 (= K-g2)",
        "50 moves rule - this rule applies to endgame situations. The 50-moves rule is in favor of the player who will play next",
        "Threefold repetition rule - no pawn moves result in three-fold repetition of the same position on the same side and the game is a draw"
    ]

    # Define the legal board positions
    legal_positions = [
        "d5 (= p-d5), c6 (= p-c6), b6 (= p-b6), a6 (= p-a6), b5 (= p-b5) and Qb2",
        "d6 (= p-d6), f4 (= f6/5)"
    ]

    # Check for illegal positions
    for illegal_position in illegal_positions:
        if illegal_position in game:
            print("Illegal position detected!")
            return

    # Check for legal positions
    for legal_position in legal_positions:
        if legal_position in game:
            return

    # If neither illegal nor legal positions are found, return the next move
    next_move = moves_so_far[-1] + "-"
    if previous_move[0] == "Q":
        next_move += "c5"
    else:
        next_move = "Qe5"
    return next_move

provider "aws" {
  region = "us-west-2"
}

# VPC setup
resource "aws_vpc" "main" {
  cidr_block           = "10.0.0.0/16"
  tags = {
    Name = "main"
  }
}

resource "aws_subnet" "main" {
  vpc_id     = aws_vpc.main.id
  cidr_block = "10.0.1.0/24"
  tags = {
    Name = "main-subnet"
  }
}

# EC2 instance setup
resource "aws_instance" "web" {
  ami           = "ami-0c55b159cbfafe1f0" # Amazon Linux 2 LTS (HVM) - Kernel 4.14, SSD Volume Type
  instance_type = "t2.micro"
  subnet_id     = aws_subnet.main.id

  tags = {
    Name = "web-server"
  }
}

# Route table setup
resource "aws_route_table" "main" {
  vpc_id = aws_vpc.main.id

  tags = {
    Name = "main-route-table"
  }
}

resource "aws_route_table_association" "a" {
  subnet_id      = aws_subnet.main.id
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.main.id
}

# Security group setup
resource "aws_security_group" "web" {
  name        = "web-sg"
  description = "Allow HTTP and SSH traffic"
  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.main.id

  ingress {
    from_port   = 80
    to_port     = 80
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }

  ingress {
    from_port   = 22
    to_port     = 22
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }

  egress {
    from_port   = 0
    to_port     = 0
    protocol    = "-1"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }
}

# Network firewall rules setup
resource "aws_network_firewall_security_group_association" "security_group" {
  subnet_id = aws_subnet.main.id
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.web.id
}

## move-generator-ai

This is an AI that takes a chess position and a fixed length set of moves and generates a sequence that leads down the moves yet continues to be legal. The MaxLength parameter can be controlled. It has a move tracker that tracks possible legal moves left at every position.

This AI works up to the 10th rank should be able to exhaustively answer theServer a few thousand positions in one second.

An optional verbose output flag is used to output to the console the generated move at the end. If the "saveToFileName" option is provided, it will write to a file instead.

It can be executed with ninja:

```bash
ninja move_gen
```
And run by

```bash
python move_gen.py

```

# Example usage
Generate 6- steps for white

```bash
python move_gen.py -e -v
```

OR

```bash
python move_gen.py -e -v -l 6  -out epaTest.csv
```

or also

```bash
python move_gen.py -e -v --links stats_links.csv
```

# Configuration
- The ai length is variable, you can modify the MaxLength parameter.
- verbose output is controlled by the verbose option. If verbose is set to false the a prompt will not appear but the output of the moves
- The file used to output link database is controlled by the saveToFileName parameter. If saveToFileName is not provided no file will be output.
- the root position parameter starts the ai at the given position. If root position is not given then the ai will start at an epa+ position with a given number of moves for a given length. If the boardLength is not given then the ai will assume a maxLength of 7

#     Ex: python move_gen.py -e -v -l 5 -out epaTest.csv
- The file that contains white's opens in FEN notation is controlled by the fileName parameter. By default the AI starts with epa (epa11.csv)

# Options

- -e functions: log-each stats
- -v verbose output on-end
- -o htmls saves html files locally with matchup ids
- --links saves html links to a file (`stats_links.csv`)
- --rank int ouputs only positions with maxUnderThreshold number of sets (defaults to None)
- --uniqueOne no duplicating id's. leaving unique too late could result in too large of number of moves, can make the Rabbit created matches much more hit/aware
- -- Starting-FEN: (FEN passing position you can the ai with)
- -- saveToFileName and -out: Create a file name here to save to
- -t time in seconds here
- -l moves length here

# Stats

- `# marathon`: long ceremony to all positions
- `# matched-only`: длинный конкурент потомковых шагов
- `# useful`: процентильный ловлящий возврат и Черная и Белая пода 연락 maje на 2.5 зДе де
- `# 2Ps`: целевого позиция шагogenic dory Draw, заблудшая числе два версия исходная, Hatodo не попахивает
- `W` white wins, `B` black wins, `D` white murine, `B` black(indisputable)
- `note index: WinRatio` correspond to GameTest with `rate = 4` (Ж плесень 'ученых') whereas `# 2Ps` allows for a `rate = 2`.5` (Ж кровать (note Ар).
